title: @node-net/netconf-server device definition
description: What a @node-net/netconf-server emulates: its YANG modules, capabilities, initial data and quirks. See docs/net-netconf-server-design.md §13.

emulates.description: The id of the @node-net/netconf client profile this device should be detected as.

modules.description: The modules the device implements. Their imports are found automatically, and the NETCONF base modules are added.

features.description: Enabled features per module. A module not listed has every feature enabled; an empty list disables them all.

deviations.description: Implemented modules that carry deviations of other modules.

importOnly.description: Modules to load but not implement.

directories.description: Directories to find modules in, relative to this file, searched before @node-net/yang's bundled IETF modules.

capabilities.description: The optional protocol capabilities the device advertises, and extras.

writableRunning.description: :writable-running. Default: true when the device has no candidate.

withDefaults.description: :with-defaults (RFC 6243), or false for none. Default basic mode explicit, with every other mode also supported.

extra.description: Extra capability URIs, advertised as written.

moduleCapabilities.description: Module capability URIs exactly as the real device writes them, replacing the generated ones.

data.description: Initial data files, relative to this file, in XML or RFC 7951 JSON.

yangLibrary.description: What the YANG library (RFC 8525) reports beyond the defaults.

modulesState.description: Also provide the deprecated modules-state container (RFC 7895), as older devices do.

quirks.description: Misbehaviours of the real device to emulate (design §13): each true (its defaults) or an object of settings, naming the @node-net/netconf client quirk it exercises. With none the server behaves as the RFCs require, and control sessions never get them.

replyWithoutMessageId.description: Replies without a message-id (exercises the client's replyWithoutMessageId).

replies.description: Which replies lose it: rpc-error replies only, or all.

invalidXmlChars.description: rpc-error messages carry a character XML 1.0 does not allow, as devices that copy CLI output do (exercises invalidXmlChars).

char.description: The character: one C0 control character other than tab, line feed and carriage return.

paddedEmptyElements.description: Empty elements in replies written across two lines (exercises paddedEmptyElements).

chunkedFramingBroken.description: Advertises base:1.1 but writes broken chunk headers, so the device works only with base:1.0 (exercises forceBaseVersion). Applies to sessions opened after it is set.

noPipelining.description: A request that arrives while another is being answered gets operation-failed (exercises maxInFlight).

slowCloseSession.description: The close-session reply comes late, or never (exercises closeTimeout).

delay.description: Milliseconds before the reply; never when absent.

subtreeFilterLimit.description: Subtree filters may go only so deep, failing with the device's own error text (exercises subtreeFilter and subtreeFilterDepth).

depth.description: Levels a filter may go down; keyed list entries straight after them don't count.

message.default: Leaf element specified which is not a key
message.description: The error-message a deeper filter gets.

candidateUnvalidated.description: Candidate edits aren't validated until commit or validate, as netopeer2 does (exercises no client quirk; referenced by the interop allowlist).
